textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a small BUNDLE OF TWO adjacent human Type II (fast-twitch) skeletal muscle fibres lying side by side, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around the structures so labels can be attached later. The illustration's own neutral dark charcoal background must extend and touch all four edges of the canvas, filling it completely corner to corner. Do NOT draw any border line, rectangle outline, frame, mat, margin band, vignette or letterbox bar around the artwork, and do NOT draw the picture as a sheet or card lying on a surface.

HOUSE LOOK — match a refined educational plate exactly: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette of soft dusty tints (never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), gentle soft shading with subtle dimensionality, and each structure its own distinct soft colour fill.

THIS IS A FAMILY PORTRAIT, NOT ONE FIBRE (most important instruction): show TWO long cylindrical fibres running side by side, parallel to each other, separated by a thin pale connective-tissue gap (endomysium), both running diagonally together across the whole frame. They represent the two related members of the human fast-twitch fibre family, and the two fibres must be VISIBLY DIFFERENT from each other, not two copies of the same tube:
- The UPPER-LEFT fibre is Type IIa: a PALE ROSE-PINK body colour (between deep red and cream), with a MODERATE number of amber-ochre mitochondria — clearly more, and slightly larger, than in its neighbour — scattered between its myofibrils in the cutaway window, and a moderately thick capillary (a crimson-cored vessel) running alongside it.
- The LOWER-RIGHT fibre is Type IIx: a PALER, near-white PINK-CREAM body colour, distinctly lighter than its neighbour, visibly the WIDER of the two fibres, with SPARSE, small, individually-scattered amber-ochre mitochondria in its cutaway window — deliberately few — and a noticeably THINNER capillary alongside it than the IIa fibre's.

CRITICAL FRAMING FIX: BOTH fibres' two ends must be CUT OFF by the canvas edges. Do NOT draw rounded end caps, full round cross-section discs, or any visible tip at either end of either fibre. Both cylinders must run diagonally corner to corner together and appear to CONTINUE beyond the frame in all four directions, as if the picture were a cropped window onto the middle of two much longer objects lying side by side, like two sliced sausages seen through a rectangular hole, never complete capsules floating with both ends visible inside the canvas. CRITICAL FRAMING CHECK: at the two diagonal corners where the bundle exits, the fibres' own body colours must fully cover the picture right into the corner, touching both edges that meet at that corner with no background-coloured triangle of empty space left over. A flat cut face, a rounded tip, or ANY margin of background between either fibre and an edge at either end is a FAIL.

MORPHOLOGY: both fibres are plain, straight, UNBRANCHED cylindrical tubes; neither forks, branches, or tapers into a Y anywhere.

SURFACE AND INTERIOR (apply to BOTH fibres identically in pattern, only differing in the colour/density points above):
- A thin teal-blue SARCOLEMMA outlines each cylinder.
- Each fibre's surface carries two distinct patterns at once, both real and both must be visible together: (1) regular narrow dark and pale bands running ACROSS the fibre, perpendicular to its long axis, repeating evenly end to end like rungs on a ladder or the rings of a hose — a fine slate-blue Z-DISC line sits at the centre of every pale band, and this transverse banding runs the ENTIRE visible length of BOTH fibres with no gaps; (2) underneath that transverse banding, fine parallel MYOFIBRIL striping runs lengthwise along each fibre's long axis, giving the surface a combed, ribbed grain within each transverse band. Both patterns are visible at once on both fibres — the transverse ladder-rung bands crossing each fibre, and the fine lengthwise myofibril grain inside each band — the way woven fabric shows both a weft and a warp.
- Along each fibre's outer rim, spaced out one after another, draw AT LEAST SIX separate oval, flattened, blue-violet NUCLEI per fibre, every single one tucked immediately under the sarcolemma at the periphery, oriented lengthwise with the fibre. Do NOT draw a single nucleus in the middle of either cell.
- In a neat long cutaway window along part of each fibre, reveal parallel MYOFIBRILS carrying the transverse striation pattern, with mitochondria scattered between them per the density difference described above (moderate + slightly larger in IIa, sparse + small in IIx), and small golden-tan GLYCOGEN GRANULE dots dusted through the sarcoplasm of both, more densely in the IIx fibre.
- Alongside each fibre, outside its sarcolemma, run one slender CAPILLARY (a thin tube with a fine crimson lumen) tracking that fibre's length — clearly thicker/denser for the IIa fibre, clearly thinner/sparser for the IIx fibre.

DO NOT draw: a single fibre alone; two identical-looking fibres with no visible colour or mitochondria difference; any branching, forking, or Y-shape; intercalated discs; a single central nucleus or any nucleus not touching the rim; deep true-red colouration on either fibre; a smooth unstriated patch anywhere along either fibre; a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella or cilia. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars or watermarks anywhere in the image. Capillaries must be smooth, thin, continuously curving vessels of a single uniform dusty-rose/crimson tone — never candy-cane, barber-pole, segmented, or bead-striped. Re-confirming: BOTH ends of BOTH fibres must be sliced off by the picture edge.
sem:
Photorealistic false-colour SCANNING ELECTRON MICROGRAPH of a small BUNDLE OF TWO adjacent human Type II (fast-twitch) skeletal muscle fibres lying side by side, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous empty margin. Fill the whole square edge to edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox bar, and do not render the image as a plate lying on a surface.

THIS IS A FAMILY PORTRAIT, NOT ONE FIBRE (most important instruction): two long, thick, perfectly UNBRANCHED cylindrical fibres resting side by side on a subtly textured flat substrate, running together diagonally across the frame, separated by a shallow groove (the connective-tissue gap between them), and cropped by the frame edge at all four ends so their great length reads clearly. SEM shows surface only, so the two fibres must be told apart PURELY BY SURFACE COLOUR AND TEXTURE:
- The UPPER-LEFT fibre (Type IIa) has a distinctly PALE ROSE-PINK false-colour surface tone.
- The LOWER-RIGHT fibre (Type IIx) has a paler, near-white PINK-CREAM false-colour surface tone, and is visibly the WIDER of the two.

CRITICAL FRAMING FIX: BOTH fibres' two ends must be CUT OFF by the canvas edges — never a rounded end cap, a full round cross-section disc, or any visible tip at either end of either fibre; both cylinders continue beyond the frame in all four directions, like two sliced sausages seen through a rectangular hole. CRITICAL FRAMING CHECK: at the two diagonal corners where the bundle exits, the fibres' own colours must fully cover the picture right into the corner, touching both edges that meet there with no background-coloured triangle left over.

Render true 3D surface relief on BOTH fibres: the surface carries many fine, closely-spaced ridges that encircle each tube like the rings on a drinking straw or the rungs of a ladder laid crosswise over a rope — each ridge runs all the way around the fibre's circumference, perpendicular to its long axis, giving a corduroy-like cross-banded texture, repeating evenly along the ENTIRE visible length of BOTH fibres with no smooth gaps. Along each fibre's flanks, spaced out one after another, show several long, shallow, oval BULGES in the surface where underlying peripheral nuclei push up against the sarcolemma — at least five or six per fibre, spread along the length. A slender capillary vessel lies alongside each fibre in the groove between them and along their outer flanks — visibly a touch more substantial next to the IIa fibre, thinner next to the IIx fibre. Crisp fine surface texture, shallow depth of field so the far ends fall softly out of focus, cool studio microscopy lighting with a gentle rim light.

False-colour palette: pale dusty rose-pink for the IIa fibre, paler dusty pink-cream for the IIx fibre, a slightly cooler rose in both fibres' ridge grooves, neutral pale grey substrate, dark uncluttered charcoal background.

DO NOT render: a single fibre alone; two fibres with no visible colour difference; any branching or Y-fork; intercalated discs; a short stubby segment that fits entirely inside the frame; a smooth unribbed patch anywhere along either fibre; deep red or grey/colourless surface tones; duplicated extra specimens; any floating debris. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, instrument data bars or watermarks anywhere in the image.

watercolor:
Hand-painted WATERCOLOUR naturalist scientific plate of a small BUNDLE OF TWO adjacent human Type II (fast-twitch) skeletal muscle fibres lying side by side, in the composition of a 19th-century scientific atlas but anatomically modern and correct. Square 1:1, 1080x1080.

PAPER RULE (most important): the warm, softly mottled AGED PAPER is the background and it must FILL THE ENTIRE FRAME, edge to edge and corner to corner, with its grain and foxing running right off all four sides. Do NOT paint the artwork as a separate sheet, card or page lying on a table, desk or any surface. NO mat, NO border, NO frame, NO drop shadow, NO torn or deckled paper edge, NO grey or dark panel around a sheet, NO vignette, NO letterbox bars.

THIS IS A FAMILY PORTRAIT, NOT ONE FIBRE (second most important instruction): paint TWO long, unbranched, cylindrical fibres side by side, parallel, together diagonally across the composition, separated by a thin pale washed gap (connective tissue), painted in rich translucent washes with fine ink linework for the outlines. The two fibres must be VISIBLY DIFFERENT in wash colour:
- UPPER-LEFT fibre = Type IIa: painted a PALE ROSE-PINK wash, with a MODERATE number of small ochre mitochondria dots (clearly more than its neighbour) scattered in its cutaway, and a moderately substantial painted capillary line with a crimson core alongside it.
- LOWER-RIGHT fibre = Type IIx: painted a paler, near-white PINK-CREAM wash, distinctly lighter than the IIa fibre and visibly the WIDER of the two, with SPARSE small ochre mitochondria dots in its cutaway, and a noticeably thinner painted capillary alongside it.

CRITICAL FRAMING FIX: BOTH fibres' two ends must be CUT OFF by the canvas edges. Do NOT paint rounded end caps, full round cross-section discs, or any visible tip at either end of either fibre. Both cylinders continue beyond the frame in all four directions, like two sliced sausages seen through a rectangular hole. CRITICAL FRAMING CHECK: at the two diagonal corners where the bundle exits, the fibres' own wash colours must fully cover the picture right into the corner, touching both edges that meet there with no bare-paper triangle left over.

Each fibre's surface carries two distinct patterns at once, both real and both must be visible together: (1) regular narrow ink-lined bands running ACROSS each fibre, perpendicular to its long axis, repeating evenly end to end like rungs on a ladder — a slightly deeper A band alternates with a paler I band, with a fine ink Z-disc line down the centre of each I band, all in register, continuing the ENTIRE visible length with no gaps; (2) underneath that, fine parallel ink MYOFIBRIL striping runs lengthwise along each fibre's long axis, giving a combed, ribbed grain within each transverse band. Both patterns visible at once on both fibres, like the weft and warp of woven fabric.

A painted cutaway along part of each fibre shows the interior carrying that same striation; along each fibre's outer edge, spaced out one after another, AT LEAST SIX separate small oval violet-washed NUCLEI per fibre, every one sitting right at the rim under the painted sarcolemma line — never a single nucleus painted in the middle; mitochondria dots per the density difference above; small golden-tan GLYCOGEN GRANULE dots stippled through the sarcoplasm, more densely in the IIx fibre; and, running alongside each fibre, one slender painted CAPILLARY line with a fine crimson core.

Muted botanical-plate palette: pale rose-pink, paler pink-cream, dusty rose, cream, ochre, golden-tan, soft slate blue and violet, on warm cream paper.

DO NOT paint: a single fibre alone; two fibres with no visible colour or mitochondria difference; any branching or Y-fork; intercalated discs; a short stubby segment fitting entirely inside the frame; a single central nucleus or any nucleus not at the rim; deep true-red or grey/colourless washes on either fibre; densely packed mitochondria on either fibre; a smooth unstriated patch anywhere along either fibre; a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella or cilia. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, handwriting, labels, arrows, scale bars, signatures or watermarks anywhere in the image. Both fibres keep a perfectly UNIFORM diameter along their whole visible length — no narrowing, pinching, necking down, tapering, or hourglassing anywhere in the middle. Capillaries must be smooth, thin, continuously curving vessels of a single uniform dusty-rose/crimson tone — never candy-cane, barber-pole, segmented, or bead-striped. Re-confirming: BOTH ends of BOTH fibres must be sliced off by the picture edge.
